section.sectionSummaryBrief: Based on the above, the Zohar's phrase "I will show him" refers to Moshe, who opened the channel for future wonders during the Exodus, though it was hidden from him.
section.t: And based on all the above, we can explain what is said in the Zohar,
"I will show him"
(wonders)
—the third-person language refers to Moshe,
for the redemption of the Exodus from Egypt was through Moshe.
And according to the above, that in the redemption of the Exodus the channel was also opened for the future redemption,
it follows
that Moshe opened the channel for the wonders that will be in the future redemption.
However, even so, this was with him in concealment.
And this is the meaning of "As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders,"
that in the future, the wonders that he opened in the Exodus from Egypt will be revealed to him.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Alternatively, the third-person "I will show him" instructs each Jew that to see future wonders, one must reveal the aspect of Moshe within, combining self-nullification of revelation with acceptance of the yoke.
section.t: Also, it can be said
that this "I will show him"
(wonders)
—the third-person language refers to Moshe,
is an instruction to every single Jew,
that in order to merit seeing the wonders of the future, it is through the revelation of the aspect of Moshe within him.

For although the self-nullification of Moshe is a self-nullification of absolute non-existence, nevertheless, the drawing down of the matter of "I will show him wonders" is through the self-nullification of acceptance of the yoke
(as explained in section 9),
nevertheless,
in order for the drawing down to be in revelation
("I will show him")
there must also be the self-nullification that stems from revelations
(through contemplation that everything before Him is considered as nothing,
and the like),
and through this there will be "I will show him wonders,"
that the wonders of the future will be in revelation,
with the coming of Mashiach our righteous one, speedily and truly.
